cohort: 20,248 participants in the Norwegian Mother and Child Cohort Study (1999-2008) without preexisting pelvic pain in pregnancy
finding: Cesarean delivery was associated with a lower risk of new-onset pelvic pain after childbirth, while operative vaginal delivery was associated with an increased risk.
mod_finding: Planned and emergency cesarean deliveries were associated with reduced odds of pelvic pain compared to unassisted vaginal delivery.
